one_line_description.value: Sentry provides a public web API for programmatically accessing the Sentry platform and managing account-level resources such as organizations, teams, and data exports.
one_line_description.quote: The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically. You can use the APIs to manage account-level resources, like organizations and teams, as well as manage and export data.

has_public_api.quote: The Sentry web API is used to access the Sentry platform programmatically.

api_type.quote: The current version of the Sentry's web API is considered v0. Our public endpoints are generally stable, but beta endpoints are subject to change.

api_breadth.value: Broad read-write HTTP/JSON API covering organizations, teams, projects, issues, events, releases and exports; versioned under /api/0/
api_breadth.quote: You can use the APIs to manage account-level resources, like organizations and teams, as well as manage and export data.

auth_methods.quote: For third-party applications that need to access Sentry on behalf of users, Sentry supports OAuth2 with the authorization code grant type.

access_model.quote: You can create authentication tokens within Sentry by creating an internal integration.

access_notes.value: Auth tokens and internal integrations are self-serve on any plan, including the free Developer plan (no sales contact or app review) - create them in Sentry settings. User-scoped personal tokens are also self-created. OAuth2 for third-party apps is gated: Sentry must register the application and asks you to contact its partnership team (partnership-platform@sentry.io). Production use still requires a Sentry org/project, but a free Developer plan exists.
access_notes.quote: These auth tokens can be created within Sentry on the "User settings" page (User settings > Personal Tokens) and assigned specific scopes.

rate_limits.quote: Each endpoint has its own maximum number of requests and window size.

webhooks.quote: Sentry uses JSON webhooks to get error notifications to your systems or services.

sdk_languages.quote: MCP Monitoring requires Node SDK version `9.46.0` or newer.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Versioned via the /api/0/ prefix (web API considered v0); public endpoints are generally stable while beta endpoints may change. No formal deprecation/sunset policy was present in the evidence.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The current version of the Sentry's web API is considered v0. Our public endpoints are generally stable, but beta endpoints are subject to change.

verdict_reason: Sentry documents a broad public web API with a stable-base /api/0/ versioning scheme, documented auth via self-created auth tokens/internal integrations, and a free Developer plan. Authentication tokens are self-serve with no sales contact, and rate limits plus webhooks are documented (including official rate-limit headers). The only gated path is OAuth2 app registration for third-party distributed apps, which requires Sentry partnership registration but is optional for token-based integrations.
main_blocker: OAuth2 app registration requires Sentry partnership team approval (token auth is self-serve)
open_questions: No documented API sandbox/test environment was found; Sentry 'environments' are data tags on events, not an isolated test API environment - confirm whether a sandbox exists.
REST classification is inferred from HTTP/JSON endpoints; the API reference page does not explicitly name the protocol.
OAuth2 for third-party apps requires Sentry to register the app via its partnership team - confirm whether this applies only to distributed public integrations or also to private single-org apps.
SDK languages were only confirmed for JavaScript/Node and Python from the evidence; the full official SDK list was not retrieved.
Numeric rate limits are not published; only the per-endpoint/per-caller mechanism and X-Sentry-Rate-Limit-* headers are documented.
Deprecation/sunset policy for API versions beyond the 'beta endpoints are subject to change' statement was not found.
Composio lists a sentry toolkit using OAUTH2 and a sentry_mcp toolkit using DCR_OAUTH; verify how Composio's OAuth flow is provisioned given Sentry's partner-registration requirement.
